stories.summary: Aaryan Ghorpade, a North Carolina student, has triumphed in a national competition with EcoRoute, a project that tracks wildlife-vehicle collision hotspots across the U.S. This innovative online tool gathers collision data and produces heat maps to assist transportation agencies in improving road safety. EcoRoute also encourages community involvement, allowing users to report wildlife sightings. Ghorpade envisions further enhancements and plans to partner with wildlife conservation organizations in his state.

stories.title: Indian family seeks help to bring back man's body after he dies from burn injuries in New Zealand on birthday
Stephen King's Maine mansion becomes a literary archive, with $2,500 writers' retreats next door
stories.summary: Stephen King and Tabitha have innovatively turned their Bangor residence into a unique archive and retreat for writers. This initiative offers aid and an inspiring atmosphere, allowing selected authors to immerse themselves in their work. The nearby Brown Mansion will serve as an additional haven, benefitting a variety of literary talents, including educators and Maine local writers.

stories.title: Streamer Feud Over Halloween: Banks slams Plaqueboymax’s ‘whiteface’ stream; questions career slide
stories.summary: Plaqueboymax’s Halloween livestream led to disagreements with Adin Ross and FaZe Banks. Adin suggested a blackface stream after seeing Max’s crew dressed as stereotypical white men. Max questioned Adin’s respect for Black culture, while Banks said Max’s costume showed disrespect towards white people. Banks also criticised Max’s content, career direction and Super Bowl halftime show ambitions, and invoked Kai Cenat.

stories.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle back to US after shameful exit from Greece; moved in with ex-husband with a hit list: Report
What led to Susie Wiles' firing within 3 days of Trump's midterm loss? 'Ice maiden' was Trump's longest serving chief of staff
stories.summary: Susie Wiles fired: Within three days of midterm rout, President Donald Trump elevated Stephen Miller to the post of Chief of Staff replacing Susie Wiles, who served the longest on the post. The decision was not out of the blue as there were speculations which the president at that time dismissed.

stories.title: How Cristiano Ronaldo turned a Madeira nightclub into an $8 million home
Who is Navneet Alag? Meet husband of newly elected Indian-American congresswoman Pia Dandiya
Idaho Supreme Court overturns ruling granting ex-partner 50% property ownership
Jewel-backed youth foundation reaches 1.6 million with mental health tools
How Abdullahs managed the rebellion: Farooq calls MLAs’ demands genuine, Omar offers to resign
Meryl Streep backs women's history education as two teachers earn award for AP course campaign
stories.summary: Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams from Sacred Heart Preparatory have pioneered an Advanced Placement course focused on women's history, garnering endorsement from 100 esteemed universities and colleges. This initiative underscores the vital role women have played throughout history. An eminent gala in Chicago on November 6, 2026, will unveil the inaugural Meryl Streep Educator Award, with proceeds dedicated to bolstering educational resources for women's history.

stories.title: India’s only floating post office gets longer working hours
Will you comply with Japanese laws? Japan plans new question for foreign visitors on entry form
US mother transfers property to son in 2003; court cancels deed after he refuses to return it
stories.summary: A New York mother who transferred her property to her son and daughter-in-law in 2003 after he promised to return it whenever asked has won a legal battle 23 years later. When the couple refused to return the property, she approached the court. A New York appeals court has now upheld the cancellation of the deed, ruling in her favour.

stories.title: London councillors reject Berkeley Homes plan after affordable housing offer falls from 40% to 12%
stories.summary: Southwark Council's planning committee voted unanimously against Berkeley Homes' revised plans for the Bermondsey Place development. The housebuilder proposed reducing affordable housing from 40 percent to just 12 percent, causing strong local opposition. Council members expressed concerns about the long timeline for home completion and questioned the developer's financial figures. Berkeley Homes highlighted rising costs and council fees as reasons for the reduced affordable housing offer.

stories.title: Court upholds sale of divorced Arkansas woman's property share after her bankruptcy filing.
stories.summary: In a landmark ruling, a federal appeals court upheld the sale of a divorced woman's stake in property located in Arkansas. The decision favored her bankruptcy trustee, overcoming objections posed by her ex-husband. He contended that the buyer's good faith was not adequately proven in prior hearings but failed to voice this concern earlier. Consequently, the property transaction with Blue Sun Capital LLC is deemed legally binding.

stories.title: '100% in favour': Trump backs AI expansion despite growing data centre backlash
‘Breaking Bad’ star Dean Norris lists California ranch for $3.2 million amid divorce and bankruptcy proceedings
stories.summary: Dean Norris has listed his expansive 11-acre ranch in Temecula for an asking price of $3,199,267 amidst ongoing divorce proceedings. His wife, Bridget, filed for divorce due to irreconcilable differences, while also pursuing joint custody of their children. Compounding their challenges, the couple's restaurant, Swing Inn Cafe, has entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Featuring an infinity pool and horse barn, the ranch attracts potential buyers seeking luxury.

stories.title: Indian student Sreeja Koya Reddy missing in Boston for 3 days; police seek public's help to trace 23-year-old
Show Hope marks 10,000 adoptions across 65 countries, surpassing its founders' original goal
stories.summary: Show Hope, the non-profit organization founded by Steven Curtis Chapman and Mary Beth in 2003, has achieved significant milestones. The charity has successfully helped over 10,000 children find permanent families through its adoption grants. In celebration of this achievement, a benefit concert will be held at the Grand Ole Opry featuring notable artists. Five dollars from each ticket sold will support the organization's ongoing programs.

stories.title: 'Convince Modi ji for SIR debate': Rahul Gandhi tells Amit Shah to stop confusing PM, shares video of remarks
PM Modi's Sule message to Sharad Pawar; 'internal tussle' in NCP: Is Maharashtra politics heading for another churn?
stories.summary: Internal conflicts within the Pawar clan has once again put the party at a crossroads. A meeting of senior NCP leaders with Union home minister Amit Shah amid reports of discontent within the party has fuelled speculations. NCP chief Sunetra Pawar has convened meetings to address unity concerns after Ajit Pawar's death. Rohit Pawar has issued a caution to the family regaridng possible BJP manoeuvres.

stories.title: 16 Canadians moved to Florida in 2022 on instruction of cult leader Liana Shanti. After years of legal battle, 3 get $56 million in defamation case
3M agrees to pay up to $7.35 billion in PFAS water contamination settlement involving 120,000 people
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, 3M has agreed to a $7.35 billion resolution for personal injury claims linked to PFAS exposure. This crucial settlement is designed to aid individuals asserting health damages from polluted water and products. The claims process is set up to fairly assess and settle cases expeditiously, with around 120,000 potential beneficiaries meeting defined eligibility criteria. This agreement marks a pivotal move toward tackling PFAS-related health problems.

stories.title: 'Directed at Delhi govt officials': Court dismisses plea seeking FIR against CM Rekha Gupta over Lord Hanuman remark
1983 Air Canada jet runs out of fuel mid-air, but pilots land safely with all 69 aboard
stories.summary: On July 23, 1983, an Air Canada Boeing 767 experienced a loss of engine power while traversing over Manitoba. With 61 passengers and 8 crew aboard, a serious fuel miscalculation by ground staff resulted in a 45 percent shortage. Remarkably, the pilots managed to glide the aircraft and executed an emergency landing on an old military track. Thankfully, everyone onboard suffered only minor injuries, and the plane was later restored.

stories.title: Michael Jordans's Wings initiative supports 4,000 scholars, awards 350 in 2025

Man Sues OpenAI Over Poison Plot: lawsuit says ChatGPT aided alleged plan; adds to AI legal scrutiny
Notary rewrites 88-year-old woman’s will to inherit her fortune
stories.summary: In a shocking case from Braunfels, an 88-year-old woman’s intention to leave her estate to charities was thwarted by a corrupt former notary who forged her will. The Limburg Regional Court imposed a two-year suspended sentence on the notary, who attributed his actions to financial stress but was ultimately deemed to have acted out of greed. His courtroom apology raises questions about the potential repercussions for the woman’s family.

stories.title: Living near a highway toll plaza? New FASTag rule offers annual pass of up to Rs 3,000, but there's a catch
stories.summary: Residents living within 20 km of National Highway toll plazas can apply for a Concessional Local Pass. The pass costs Rs 1,500 or Rs 3,000 annually, depending on the plaza's location. To qualify, motorists must have a functional FASTag, and their vehicle must be non-commercial. The scheme aims to reduce toll expenses for eligible residents but has specific restrictions.

stories.title: Trump had demanded that Harmeet K Dhillon be fired after he watched her on 60 Minutes on October 18: Report
North Carolina court revives roofing firm's lawsuits against insurers over unpaid storm repairs
stories.summary: A North Carolina appeals court has reinstated lawsuits from Piedmont Roofing Services against various major insurance companies. Overturning an earlier trial judge's dismissal of breach of contract claims, the court concluded that sufficient grounds exist for the roofing company to pursue its claims. This ruling sheds light on the intricate legal issues related to the transfer of insurance rights in property damage situations.

stories.title: Evening Newswrap: Panic as Karmabhoomi Express catches fire in Punjab; bomb threats to Bombay HC, BSE and Amitabh Bachchan’s residence, and more
'Your tacit approval?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin questions Rahul Gandhi over Jharkhand Congress leader's 'Nepal-Bangladesh' remark
Eva Longoria-backed charity supports 100+ children at Vietnam orphanage, expands plans to Spain therapy centre
stories.summary: Since 2018, the Global Gift Foundation has championed the Quang Chau Orphanage, now known as Casa Ángeles, providing care to over 100 needy children. This initiative, bolstered by funds from the Global Gift Gala in Paris, also supports the Casa Ángeles therapy centre in Spain. Through engaging performances and a vibrant auction, the event helps sustain vital projects aimed at uplifting vulnerable communities.

stories.title: At 9, she started feeding hungry children; now her nonprofit has reached over 110,000 people
stories.summary: New Jersey teenager Anakh Sawhney started Rice Kids in 2018, aged nine, to provide meals to hungry children. Her nonprofit has since supported more than 110,000 people across five US states and parts of India through food, education, healthcare and other essential resources. More than half of the students supported by the organisation in India have returned to mainstream education.

stories.title: The watchman and the log scale
Democrats win Congress but Trump's final 2 years could be the most explosive yet
Michigan brother ploughs landscaped strip beside sibling's home, triggering bitter land dispute
stories.summary: A Michigan appeals court revived a couple's claim over a 0.13-acre strip allegedly landscaped by their family for years. The dispute began after the husband's brother ploughed the land in 2022. The court ruled that a 1991 foreclosure judgment did not prevent the boundary claim, while leaving the $5,364.44 award for trespass and waste undisturbed.

stories.title: New York buyer loses $1 million lawsuit after demanding $270,000 cut on $550,000 Bronx home deal
stories.summary: A man from New York made a cash offer for a dilapidated home in the Bronx, agreeing to accept it in its current state. After finding additional issues just days before the closing, he sought a considerable price decrease. The seller declined, referring to the contract terms and previous property condition disclosures.

stories.title: US start-up plans to sell sunlight at night with India's Skyroot Aerospace
'1,800 fake AI books, inflated prices': Periyar library pits CM Vijay against DMK
stories.summary: In a heated exchange, Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay pointed fingers at the former DMK administration for alleged corruption linked to library book purchases. It has come to light that almost 1,800 artificially generated books were bought at excessive prices. Author Perumal Murugan raised concerns, leading Congress's Manickam Tagore to insist on a full inquiry.

stories.title: Milo Ventimiglia says family is settled in new home after losing two houses in LA fires
stories.summary: Milo Ventimiglia and wife Jarah Mariano lost their home and another house under construction in the January 2025 Los Angeles fires, when she was 38 weeks pregnant. Nearly two years later, the actor says the family has settled into a new home with their two children, while reflecting on the loss, memories and rebuilding their lives.

stories.title: 'Inviting death': Jharkhand tribal leader dies by suicide after emotional Facebook Live post
stories.summary: Nisha Kumari Bhagat, a prominent tribal leader in Jharkhand, was tragically found dead at her home in Ranchi. Just hours prior, she had gone live on Facebook, voicing concerns about threats from governmental bodies and land brokers. While police have indicated a possible suicide, they are actively probing the details surrounding her untimely death.

stories.title: CBI books Future Retail Ltd, key promoters in Rs 904-crore bank fraud case
stories.summary: CBI has registered a major bank fraud concerning Future Retail Ltd. and its top executives for bank fraud. This case, involving Rs 904 crore, follows a complaint from State Bank of India regarding fund misappropriation. Search operations were conducted at various locations linked to the firm's promoters, leading to the recovery of important documents. The company reportedly diverted bank funds through associated entities without using them for the intended purposes.

stories.title: You can own the world and still feel poor: Aruna Lohia Goenka on the magic of abundance
EC gives voters excluded from draft electoral rolls in 7 states another chance to apply
SC ends decades-old power tussle, Himachal to get 11,973 MU from Punjab, Haryana
OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions but leaves pending cases open
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has clarified that its March ruling will not impact completed appointments or promotions. Cases still pending will be examined individually by the courts based on merit and eligibility. The government expressed concerns that retrospective application could unsettle established positions and admissions. It sought two years to establish a uniform creamy layer mechanism across various sectors.

stories.title: Karmabhoomi Express passengers panic as moving train catches fire in Punjab
'Will be dealt with iron hand': SC issues contempt notice to Kerala Congress over controversial CJI post
2013 Tehelka rape case: SC refuses to suspend Tarun Tejpal's 10-year jail term
IMA asks CBFC to deny certification to Sunny Deol-starrer, flags glorification of violence against doctors
stories.summary: The Indian Medical Association has raised concerns about the film Suryaa, which they claim glorifies violence against healthcare workers. They argue that certain scenes depict a father taking revenge on doctors, raising ethical issues. The IMA provided data on increased workplace violence against healthcare professionals in recent years. They have requested that the Central Board of Film Certification deny certification based on these representations.

stories.title: 'Bomb on board': How three minute warning changed Dublin to Rome Aer Lingus flight's route
‘Vote gone, rights gone’: Rahul alleges BJP conspiracy in schemes linked with voter ID instead of Aadhaar
NC rebellion calms down at Abdullahs’ door; Omar’s advisor Wani is in London as Speaker accepts Ruhullah’s resignation
Najib Royal Pardon House Arrest: Party pays 50mn ringgit fine; transfer date unclear
stories.summary: Najib Razak is anticipated to transition from prison to house arrest after a fine has been paid. His political party, the United Malays National Organisation, successfully gathered the required funds through a fundraising initiative, satisfying a crucial condition for his royal pardon from Malaysia's king. Police have been stationed outside Najib's Kuala Lumpur residence in preparation for the transfer, although authorities have not disclosed the precise timing of the move.

stories.title: Rocky Balboa, Superman Cash, Fat Boy: Trio charged for using AI to steal $129 million in US
stories.summary: A trio known as 'Rocky Balboa', 'Superman Cash', and 'Fat Boy' has been charged with orchestrating a massive fraud scheme. Utilizing artificial intelligence, they impersonated corporate leaders and lawyers, targeting the accounting departments of various businesses. Over the course of 18 months, they allegedly swindled around $129 million from victims across the globe. They are facing serious allegations such as wire fraud, identity theft, and money laundering.

stories.title: Texas court upholds $7.11m award to aide injured while moving 300-pound patient
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court upheld a nursing facility's liability after a CNA was injured while transferring a patient weighing over 300 pounds in 2016. It upheld most of the $7.11 million jury award but proposed reducing future medical expenses by $264,448.51 or ordering a new trial.

stories.title: New York man claims mother and sister broke promises over father's Pennsylvania property and Long Island home after his death in Saudi Arabia; 16 years later, US court dismisses lawsuit
stories.summary: In a recent ruling, Saad Ahmed's lawsuit challenging his mother and sister over inheritance was dismissed by a New York court. The court found that many of his claims were filed too late, beyond the legal deadlines. Ahmed had accused his family of not honoring property transfer agreements, resulting in disputes. The appellate court affirmed the dismissal, stressing the critical nature of adhering to legal timelines in inheritance matters.

stories.title: For decades, physicists assumed black holes can merge but cannot split; new calculations suggest a black hole spinning near its maximum speed might break in two, though nobody has ever observed it happening.
stories.summary: Recent theoretical study explores whether rapidly spinning black holes can split into two smaller black holes. Scientists have long believed that black holes are incapable of splitting due to entropy and the area theorem. The research proposes that under specific conditions, a spinning black hole could theoretically divide without violating physical laws. It introduces the concept of a pair-of-pants topology to describe this unusual scenario.

‘AQI data fraud can cost lives’: Saurabh Bharadwaj accuses Delhi government of misleading people
'NC has never been broken, will never be broken': Farooq Abdullah after meeting disgruntled MLAs
A man jailed for 46 months for tricking 12,600 people into donating $106,000 to a fake charity
Bob Dylan donated all royalties from his 2009 Christmas album to fight hunger
Jharkhand High Court quashes state government's decision to cancel JSSC CGL exam
stories.summary: The Jharkhand High Court has set aside the government's cancellation of the JSSC CGL examination. This ruling comes after candidates protested against the decision and alleged irregularities. The government had previously cancelled multiple recruitment examinations amidst public outcry over these allegations. Additionally, two individuals were arrested by the Criminal Investigation Department related to examination irregularities. Ongoing legal proceedings continue as candidates seek justice and reform in recruitment processes.

stories.title: ‘Hope you are enjoying Delhi weather’: CJI blames vehicles as SC takes up air pollution case
North Dakota ranchers take $383,375 legal fee fight against pipeline firm to US Supreme Court
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court will hear a dispute involving North Dakota ranchers and WBI Energy Transmission over $383,375.76 in legal fees. The justices will decide whether state or federal law governs compensation when private natural gas companies acquire land through eminent domain.

stories.title: Shaquille O’Neal-backed youth centre attracts 400+ children after $1.1 million makeover
stories.summary: Shaquille O’Neal’s foundation has successfully transformed a dilapidated middle school in Henry County into a vibrant Boys and Girls Club. With a renovation budget of $1.1 million, the facility now features improved educational and recreational spaces. Within its first year, it welcomed over 400 children, providing essential youth programs designed to foster safe, nurturing environments for the community’s young people.

stories.title: Judge Halts Arch Construction: US court blocks Trump monument for 14 days; veterans’ suits proceed
stories.summary: A federal judge has placed a temporary hold on the construction of a proposed triumphal arch meant to celebrate American independence. Approved by the National Capital Planning Commission, the monument faced opposition from Vietnam War veterans and local entities, who argued it lacked necessary permissions. As legal disputes unfold, the project’s momentum is halted for two weeks, raising alarms over potential environmental impacts and increased traffic in the area.

stories.title: 1 officer killed, 3 injured as gunman opens fire on police in Colorado
North Carolina farm builds 7 tiny homes inspired by a woman who spent 27 years in prison
'Jantar Mantar in Kochi': Actor Prakash Raj calls for anti-SIR protest on Saturday
Ranjeev Puri makes history as first Indian-American elected Michigan House Speaker
stories.summary: Ranjeev Puri's election as Speaker of the Michigan House of Representatives for the 2027-28 term signifies a historic milestone, marking the first instance of Indian origin in such a prominent role. Expressing gratitude to his peers, Puri highlighted the achievement's significance for his family. His background in Barack Obama's campaigns and the automotive sector fuels his commitment to lowering household expenses and uplifting South Asian communities.

stories.title: Wendy’s rejects billionaire Nelson Peltz’s $1.4 billion takeover bid, adopts ‘poison pill’ defence as burger chain shuts hundreds of US outlets
stories.summary: Wendy's has rejected a takeover proposal valued at $1.4 billion from billionaire investor Nelson Peltz. The fast-food chain argued that the offer undervalues its long-term growth potential, prompting the adoption of a shareholder rights plan. This defensive strategy is designed to protect the company from unwanted acquisition attempts. Wendy's has been facing declining sales and rising operational costs in the competitive fast-food market.

stories.title: After years of flooding, Philippine village turns to bamboo, oyster shells and coconut waste to keep rising waters at bay
stories.summary: Pamarawan village in the Philippines has embraced an innovative coastal defense system to tackle flooding challenges. This initiative incorporates natural materials such as bamboo poles, oyster shells, and coconut husks to fortify against powerful waves and prevent sediment displacement. Remarkably, there have been no flooding incidents reported for almost two years since the project's inception, prompting officials to explore similar setups for other flood-threatened areas.

stories.title: Trump-Kim reset after midterm blow? Why North Korea may hold the cards
Two Iowa families donate 21 acres for wildlife and public recreation
Centre eases immigration rules for Pakistani, Afghan minorities and other foreign nationals
Denzel Washington helped save August Wilson's childhood home, now an arts centre
Another attack on Iran soon? Trump meets top security advisers after midterm elections
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump held meetings to evaluate potential military operations against Iran's nuclear program. While considering various options, Trump indicated that decisions would be made soon regarding escalating military action. The US Central Command is preparing for possible renewed combat operations in the region, coinciding with the new moon conditions. Iranian officials have communicated their conditions for negotiations to international partners, seeking confidence-building measures.

Oregon court now upholds $810,000 award over 2018 tree clearing beyond a neighbour's property line
stories.summary: In an Oregon land dispute, a property owner accused their neighbor of intentionally clearing land past established boundaries. A jury sided with the plaintiff, awarding them $810,000 in damages. The court upheld this decision, indicating that the defendants failed to provide valid evidence to counter their liability, while also noting that Bosma was aware of the boundary issues before the clearing took place.

stories.title: Julia Child Home Sells: former Cambridge house fetches $6.525 million; kitchen lives on at Smithsonian
stories.summary: Julia Child’s iconic home in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has found a new owner for $6.525 million. This historic residence, adored for its connection to Child's culinary shows, has seen extensive renovations. The original kitchen, however, remains untouched and is now a cherished exhibit at the Smithsonian Museum. To honor her legacy, a commemorative plaque is set to be installed at the site, ensuring that Child's influence on cooking continues.

stories.title: US wildlife teams surveyed six offshore islands for invasive species, finding rats on five and iguanas on one; the results will guide future work to protect nesting seabirds
stories.summary: Recent surveys in the U.S. Virgin Islands have identified invasive species on several offshore cays. Black rats and green iguanas pose significant threats to local seabird populations, such as the red-billed tropicbird. Conservationists are now evaluating strategies to eradicate these non-native animals from the islands. Removal efforts could lead to improved nesting conditions for seabirds in the future. Successful initiatives may help restore these vital habitats for future generations.

stories.title: Day after militants killing, Manipur launches search and cordon operations
Opposition planning unrest, says BJP after TV channel sting
Youth Cong suspends 300 for no-show at Rahul's Delhi rally
Georgia court upholds waste facility permit as 97 planned townhomes still unbuilt at permit filing
stories.summary: A developer in Bartow County, Georgia challenged a permit for a nearby waste processing facility. The county approved the permit despite concerns that it violated zoning restrictions. The developer argued that their planned townhomes should receive protection under existing zoning laws. However, the court found that the definitions of residential dwellings applied only to already constructed buildings. Ultimately, the appeals court upheld the permit, allowing the waste facility to operate.

stories.title: Special summary roll revision in 6 states, UTs; draft on Nov 30
Luke Bryan's Farm Tour awards 97 college scholarships and helps provide 11 million meals since 2009
stories.summary: Since its inception in 2009, Luke Bryan's Farm Tour has championed educational opportunities by awarding 97 scholarships and supplying over 11 million meals for needy families. Partnering with Bayer’s #HerestotheFarmer campaign, the initiative bridges support between farming families and communities. Attendees also donated nearly 20,000 pounds of food to hunger-relief efforts, underscoring a commitment to enhancing education and food accessibility in agricultural areas nationwide.

stories.title: She runs a Caribbean takeaway in England and gives free meals to people who cannot afford them; 71-year-old Florence ‘Mama Flo’ Coke has become a local hero.
stories.summary: Florence Coke runs a Caribbean takeaway in Stockport, where she offers free meals for the needy. She has been inspired by her parents' tradition of helping the poor in Jamaica. During the COVID-19 crisis, she continued to feed struggling families with free meals and food parcels. Recently, she was recognized with a Local Hero award for her community service efforts.

24-hour deadline starts with detention: SC
Washington court upholds deal after couple split again, leaving wife without bank and stock assets
stories.summary: A couple from Washington navigated a messy divorce settlement only to remarry, before the cycle of separation began once more. The court upheld an arbitration ruling that favored William Gibbs, denying Joy the assets previously awarded. Although Joy retained some funds from her BNY Mellon 401(k), she forfeited half of the USAA accounts and restricted stock units.

stories.title: Texas Farm Funds Scholarships: Donated land backs Gruver High students; many are first-generation grads
stories.summary: In Gruver, Texas, a remarkable farming initiative has turned inherited land into a thriving source of scholarship funds for local students. By pooling their resources, farmers and community members cultivate crops that have raised around $3 million for education since 2012, benefitting nearly 300 students, including first-generation college graduates like Sydney Ortiz and Rhett Sparks.

stories.title: ‘I guess I’m dead’: Tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson's chilling post resurfaces
stories.summary: In a heartbreaking incident, tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson and his family lost their lives in a Florida plane crash on November 1, 2026. The tragedy claimed all nine individuals aboard the private jet. Robinson, known for his sarcastic social media presence, previously founded notable marketing technology companies. The National Transportation Safety Board has initiated an investigation into the cause of the fatal accident.

Minister alleges foreign funding, CJP counters
‘Speedy trial is a fundamental right’: SC says Constitution has primacy over special laws
Cops to give 7-day notice to Akoijam before action
Pennsylvania court upholds borough's duty to maintain steps after 130 years of public use
stories.summary: A couple from Jim Thorpe filed a lawsuit against their borough regarding the maintenance of public steps. They argued that the borough had historically maintained the steps, which had been used for over 130 years. The Commonwealth Court upheld the lower court's ruling that affirmed the borough's maintenance obligation. Evidence included historical records showing the borough's involvement in repairs and maintenance over the years.

stories.title: A British family doctor was convicted of murdering 15 patients
stories.summary: Harold Shipman, a general practitioner in England, was infamously convicted for the murder of numerous patients. His reputation as a trusted doctor gave him unfettered access to the homes of vulnerable elderly individuals, leading to a devastating series of crimes. An extensive investigation later uncovered that Shipman was linked to the deaths of at least 215 people over many years.

stories.title: Christopher Plummer's widow donates land for 750-acre nature preserve
California court allows grandfather five-minute monthly calls, rejects mother's $17,193 fee bid
stories.summary: Timothy S sought court-ordered visitation with his granddaughter after Sarah H regained custody of the children. He had raised the older child for nearly two years prior to this change in custody. The trial court allowed only a brief monthly telephone call while denying Sarah's request for legal fees tied to the case. California's Court of Appeal upheld this decision, affirming the lower court's interpretation of the law.

stories.title: Jen Lilley revives Christmas Is Not Cancelled toy drive for kids
stories.summary: Jen Lilley, the acclaimed actress, has relaunched her Christmas Is Not Cancelled campaign to aid children in need, setting a goal of delivering 20,000 gifts to underprivileged youth this Christmas. By letting parents select the gifts, the initiative preserves their dignity. Furthermore, podcaster Shawn Ryan's generous $30,000 donation will provide bikes and scooters. The campaign is now a nonprofit, making financial contributions tax-deductible.

stories.title: NASA's Hubble studied dwarf galaxies and found they kept just 11% of the oxygen made by their stars
stories.summary: A recent investigation revealed that dwarf galaxies only retain an average of 11% of the oxygen generated by their stars. The remaining oxygen likely escapes into space during powerful supernova explosions. This finding indicates that smaller galaxies have greater difficulty retaining their materials than previously believed. Researchers plan to conduct further studies to examine where this missing oxygen ultimately ends up.

Arizona appeals court upholds divorce asset division
stories.summary: An Arizona couple, married in 2016, built three businesses before filing for divorce in 2023. During the divorce, the husband disputed a business valuation and claimed loans as marital debt. The court found his loan documentation lacking credibility and upheld a valuation of $305,800. After a trial, the court awarded businesses to the wife and denied the husband's claims about wasted funds.

stories.title: Two brothers find ultra-rare Tom Brady card in $30 box
stories.summary: Lucas and Trevor Martell bought three boxes of sports cards and discovered a rare one-of-one card. The card features Tom Brady and could be worth over $150,000. This unexpected find has significantly impacted their financial situation and future plans. Lucas intends to pay off medical bills and help his grandmother using the potential earnings. The brothers also plan to start their own trading card business together for the future.

stories.title: US study finds eating one avocado & mango every day improves blood vessel function in prediabetic adults
stories.summary: A new research study indicates that integrating mango and avocado into your daily diet may significantly improve heart health. Focused on adults with prediabetes, this study monitored the effects of these fruits over eight weeks with controlled calorie intake. Results showed enhanced blood vessel performance and lowered blood pressure in male participants, highlighting the cardiovascular advantages of incorporating these nutritious fruits into your meals.

stories.title: Backyard Railway Village: Chicago family turns garden into miniature town; hobby draws visitors
stories.summary: Over two decades, a Chicago family's backyard has transformed into a vibrant miniature railway town. What began as a modest garden endeavor blossomed into a captivating landscape filled with elaborate buildings and model trains. Despite initial worries about sacrificing garden space, family members embraced the hobby, turning their yard into a destination for train enthusiasts, while inspiring younger generations to explore the joys of model railroading.

stories.title: ‘Expect new dynamics’: Ukraine hopes for more support after Democrats sweep midterms
stories.summary: Ukraine anticipates enhanced military and financial assistance from the United States after the midterm elections. Foreign minister Andrii Sybiha expressed hope for new dynamics and support from the incoming Democratic majority. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy acknowledged the Democrats' vocal backing of Ukraine since their election success. This shift in power could enable legislation favoring aid to Ukraine despite previous limitations.

stories.title: 'Memory of the world': Rajatarangini, Mahabharata & Arthashastra get UN recognition

Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata', and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' received this recognition recently. These inscriptions reflect various aspects of India's intellectual traditions, including historical writing and governance. This announcement follows India's previous regional register recognitions in 2024 for other literary works. The initiative aims to preserve and digitise India's manuscript heritage for future generations.

The activists pointed out the looming deadline for submitting new bail applications as established by the Supreme Court.

stories.title: How Rory McIlroy’s £1 million gift helped Daisy Lodge
stories.summary: Rory McIlroy donated £1 million to establish Daisy Lodge, a center for families with children suffering from cancer. Since its opening in 2014, over 4,000 families have benefited from therapeutic short breaks at the lodge. The center provides support through workshops and complementary therapies while creating a space for families to connect. Tragically, some families have also received bereavement support following the loss of loved ones.

The Michigan Court of Appeals dismissed his case, ruling that the issue had already been decided.

stories.title: 'We are doing what the government won't': Greenpeace dumps nine giant boulders into the North Sea to create a 45-square-mile underwater 'rock barrier' against industrial fishing
stories.summary: Environmental activists from Greenpeace have deployed nine limestone boulders in the Southern North Sea to prevent bottom trawling. This underwater barrier aims to protect marine biodiversity, particularly harbour porpoises affected by industrial fishing. Greenpeace argues that government protections have been insufficient to shield marine habitats from destructive fishing methods. The deployment of boulders took place without a marine licence, raising regulatory concerns.

stories.summary: An Iowa landlord, asserting a $700,000 loss from a Ponzi scheme, sought to reduce his divorce payment but was unsuccessful. The Iowa Court of Appeals confirmed the trial court's $351,446 ruling. The husband contended his premarital assets should remain separate; however, the court determined these assets were commingled and part of the marital estate. This case emphasizes the necessity for clear marital property agreements.

stories.title: Hardeep Singh Puri elected unopposed to Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh
stories.summary: Hardeep Singh Puri was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh after other candidates failed to qualify. The nominations of Rajkumar Lohani and Kante Sayanna were rejected for not meeting necessary requirements. Puri's election follows the resignation of Union minister of state L Murugan in mid-October. Hemant Khandelwal, among other officials, was present when Puri collected his election certificate.

The former Prime Minister is aware of the risks associated with her return, including potential arrest or worse. Hasina's Awami League party has been banned, resulting in widespread political repression and violence against its members. She expressed concerns over the rising influence of extremist groups in the current political climate.

US woman says co-op staff took her pets, hid dog's whereabouts; court allows lawsuit
stories.summary: A New York woman who accused co-op employees of entering her apartment without permission, removing her dog and cat, and concealing her dog's whereabouts can continue pursuing two legal claims. Nearly three years after the incident, an appeals court allowed her trespass and emotional distress claims to proceed. Court records indicated that her dog was euthanised after spending nearly two months at a shelter.

stories.summary: An effort to save a 191-acre parcel in Indiana led to the protection of nearly 4,000 acres. The land was acquired to prevent fragmentation and protect wildlife habitats in the area. Various organizations and public agencies collaborated to complete the acquisition. The Busseron Creek Fish and Wildlife Area opened to the public in April 2025 for outdoor recreation.

stories.title: Titanic's owners received $5 million within 30 days of the sinking; 114 years later, original insurance certificate resurfaces and could sell for $67,000
stories.summary: An authentic insurance document related to the Titanic's last journey is slated for auction in Britain. This significant paperwork details the insurance sought mere weeks before the 1912 sinking. The owners received their payout shortly after the tragedy, contrasting sharply with the delays faced by bereaved families. The piece also underscores the important insurance arrangements for the Titanic, along with a selection of other artifacts that commemorate its storied past.

stories.summary: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered Earth's atmosphere after 22 years in orbit, ending its mission. Swift was crucial for understanding gamma-ray bursts and other cosmic events, detecting over 2,000 bursts. The spacecraft's orbit deteriorated due to increased solar activity, leading to its uncontrolled descent. NASA attempted a rescue operation, but it ultimately failed, resulting in its re-entry on November 4, 2026.

stories.title: Filipino engineer wins £30,000 award for sensor that detects hidden earthquake damage in buildings
stories.summary: A Filipino structural engineer has won the 2026 James Dyson Global Sustainability Award and £30,000 for developing Sentinel, a sensor that detects hidden damage in buildings after earthquakes. Developed by Aldrei Ong, the technology uses self-sensing concrete to identify cracks and monitor structural changes. The invention could help engineers assess potentially unsafe buildings more quickly and reduce the risk of collapse.

stories.title: Nine people set out for a one-hour boat trip in Micronesia; three months and 5,400 km later, villagers in Kiribati rescued five survivors
stories.summary: In July, a boat with nine individuals vanished during its voyage between islands in Micronesia. The US Coast Guard launched a ten-day search, but no clues were found. Miraculously, nearly three months later, five survivors emerged on a Kiribati island, a staggering 5,400 kilometers from where they set sail. After enduring severe dehydration and malnutrition, they received medical attention.

stories.title: Detroit man turns two rubber bands into 11,578-pound ball, breaking Guinness World Record after 11 years
stories.summary: Claude P. Moore began his rubber band ball project in 2015, starting with two rubber bands. Over eleven years, he built the ball to an impressive 11,578 pounds, surpassing the previous record. Friends and family supported him throughout this extensive journey, helping transport the enormous ball for its official measurement. The record was confirmed in August 2026 by Guinness World Records during a public ceremony.

stories.title: Joshua Wong Sentencing: activist gets fresh 10-year NSL term; warns against dissent

Yet, despite being behind bars, Wong continues to inspire a new generation of pro-democracy advocates in Hong Kong.

stories.summary: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington has recently finished a significant renovation, but not without its fair share of headaches. stories.title: Michigan neighbours win $55,750 over lakefront work despite lacking any written easement in court dispute
stories.summary: Legal issues arose for Jeremy and Ivanna Leffring when their neighbors placed a 'No Trespassing' sign on what they considered shared property. The Michigan Court of Appeals favored the Leffrings, granting them $55,750 for their improvements while asserting that no formal easement could be enforced.

stories.title: Chinese genetic sequencing firm Novogene sues Pentagon over military blacklist
stories.summary: Novogene has pointed out that its US subsidiary employs around 180 people at its Sacramento office and sequencing facilities in Sacramento, California, and Beaverton, Oregon. Additionally, they introduced the Argote Award Scholarship to recognize and reward the remarkable bravery of those who come to the aid of others.

stories.title: Texas court reopens Houston home ownership dispute after foreclosure and reverse mortgage
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court has reopened a lengthy dispute over home ownership in Houston, which has complicated legal issues. The case involves multiple foreclosures, reverse mortgages, and unclear ownership claims spanning twenty-five years. Key questions remain about the validity of a 2011 mortgage after a previous foreclosure occurred in 2001. This ruling requires lower courts to thoroughly examine competing ownership claims before making decisions.

stories.title: UN report finds huge gap in adaptation finance ahead of COP31

Rich countries' collective pledge could only reach $85-120 billion each year by 2035. While current financial contributions are around $28.2-31.7 billion, this is still inadequate. UN Environment Programme emphasizes the urgent need for increased adaptation financing and overcoming institutional barriers. Action on climate adaptation is essential to mitigate worsening impacts from extreme weather events.

stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy awarded Melania Trump the Order of Princess Olga for her humanitarian work. She was instrumental in organizing a humanitarian evacuation from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky. An important ceasefire allowed nearly 800 residents to access emergency supplies and evacuate safely. Melania Trump is hosting representatives from both Russia and Ukraine to discuss the ceasefire efforts.

King Charles sold racehorse months before it won Melbourne Cup for new owners
stories.summary: Point of Law, a three-year-old former charge of King Charles III, triumphed in the prestigious Melbourne Cup at Flemington. Trainer Ciaron Maher celebrated an extraordinary trifecta as his horses secured the top three spots. This victory followed Point of Law's stunning debut triumph at the Geelong Cup, building great anticipation for the Melbourne Cup.

stories.title: A teenager tending livestock near DeadSea threw a stone into a cave; discovering DeadSeaScrolls
stories.summary: In 1947, a Bedouin shepherd stumbled upon the Dead Sea Scrolls while searching for stray animals. This discovery consisted of numerous ancient manuscripts that greatly impacted historical and religious studies. The manuscripts date back to the Second Temple period, offering insights into diverse Jewish beliefs and practices. Researchers continue to piece together fragments to reveal their contents and historical significance.

stories.title: ‘Habibi, call me Senator’: Abdul El-Sayed mocks Trump, Vance in victory speech
stories.summary: Abdul El-Sayed won the Michigan Senate race against Republican Mike Rogers, marking a significant milestone in history. His victory speech included pointed remarks aimed at both Vice President JD Vance and former President Trump. El-Sayed's campaign focused on progressive issues such as universal healthcare and criticized outside influence in elections. The election was closely contested, with substantial spending from various interest groups.

stories.title: A 3,800-year-old woman once wrote a frustrated letter to her husband complaining about a debtor
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, Anna-anna, an ancient Anatolian woman, documented her struggle to reclaim silver from her husband Ennum-Aššur's debtor, Laqēpum. Her poignant letter lay untouched for nearly 4,000 years until researchers utilized cutting-edge technology, revealing its secrets without causing damage. This innovative approach showcases the profound connections found in ancient communications, shedding light on economic and personal dynamics of the past.

stories.title: 'Debate in Parliament': Himanta Sarma hits back at Rahul Gandhi's challenge to PM Modi
stories.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's proposal for a public debate with Prime Minister Modi. Sarma emphasized that such discussions should occur in Parliament, not publicly. He challenged Gandhi to raise various critical issues like Bofors and the Bhopal Gas Tragedy during parliamentary sessions. Rahul Gandhi had expressed a desire for a debate to address national connections and financial matters.

stories.title: Patagonia sues drag queen Pattie Gonia, seeks just $1 in damages
Wisconsin man turns discarded roadside wood into all 32 NFL team logos after 700 hours of work
stories.summary: Ike Wynter, a Wisconsin wood artist, transformed discarded furniture into all 32 NFL team logos. His project, started in 2016, took over 700 hours to complete while attracting attention from the NFL. The logos were displayed at the 2025 NFL Draft held at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Wynter connected personally with the Buffalo Bills logo, honoring his late grandfather who played for the team.

stories.title: How TheBurntPeanut turned a small gaming channel into a streaming sensation after making one major change to his content
stories.summary: TheBurntPeanut transformed his streaming career by adopting a humorous approach with a virtual peanut avatar. He initially struggled to gain viewers while making serious gaming guides for Escape from Tarkov. His change to a funny streaming style significantly increased his audience and popularity over time. The launch of ARC Raiders further contributed to his success as he became a well-known figure among gamers.

stories.title: PM Modi calls Sharad Pawar; advises complete rest
Faith Evans faces $12.5 million court order in Biggie's estate dispute
UK man jailed for four years over £708,750 fake Gift Aid claims using 716 donors
Just 11 survived after a predator introduced to fight garden pests nearly wiped them out: Hawaii’s rare tree snails return to the wild after 33 years
stories.summary: After years of dedicated conservation work, the O‘ahu tree snail has made a triumphant return to Hawaii's stunning Ko‘olau Mountains. Since rescuing the last of the species in 1991 and breeding them to over 1,000 individuals, conservationists have created a safe habitat that shields them from invasive threats. Despite this success, the long-term survival of these snails remains uncertain, necessitating continuous monitoring and further breeding efforts.

stories.title: When London Bridge was rebuilt in Arizona, workers numbered granite stones before dismantling it
stories.summary: London Bridge has a storied past marked by numerous reconstructions due to various calamities. In a striking turn of events, the City of London sold the iconic bridge to American entrepreneur Robert McCulloch for $2.46 million in 1968. The bridge was carefully reassembled in Lake Havasu City, featuring a hollow core designed to accommodate modern traffic.

stories.title: Floyd Mayweather ordered to pay $340K in Manhattan rent dispute
Historic US midterms: Black, Indigenous, Latina & LGBTQ leaders win key races
stories.summary: The 2026 US midterm elections have led to historic firsts in gubernatorial and Senate races across the nation. Notable victories include the first Black woman governor in US history and the first Native American woman governor. The election of Texas' first Latina governor and Florida's first Black governor also signify progress in representation. Additionally, Minnesota has elected its first woman governor, further enhancing diversity in leadership roles.

stories.title: North Korea fires missiles hours after rejecting US accusations over Binance hack
stories.summary: North Korea recently fired multiple missiles towards its eastern waters, indicating rising tensions with South Korea and the US. This action followed North Korea's denial of involvement in a significant cryptocurrency hack attributed to its hackers by the FBI. Kim Yo Jong criticized US accusations as part of a hostile policy and refused dialogue until it changes.

stories.title: FIR against Prashant Bhushan for sharing fake video of Russian minister criticising India
US elections: K Bottoms makes history as first Black woman governor, flips Georgia seat
stories.summary: Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected governor of Georgia after defeating Rick Jackson in the recent election. Her victory signifies a historic moment as she becomes the first Black woman to hold this position. Bottoms focused her campaign on economic issues, pledging to expand Medicaid and raise the minimum wage. Jackson's significant campaign spending did not prevent his defeat despite his attacks on Bottoms' record.

Rank-based merit list to replace percentile for NEET PG: Panel to SC
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has officially approved a shift from a percentile to a rank-based system for NEET admissions, which aims to improve the current postgraduate medical course admission process. This change comes amid concerns over the possible decrease in qualifying scores for NEET-PG 2025. The commission is focused on preserving the integrity of medical examinations and has also suggested equitable salary structures for medical residents.

stories.title: Indian tourist killed, PIO injured as copters collide during Everest rescue
Take on Modi in Parliament, FM Sitharaman tells Rahul Gandhi on debate challenge
Still waiting for a debate: Rahul Gandhi to PM Modi
British wedding venue evacuated after workers uncover five World War II bombs while digging for solar panels; guests and residents forced to flee
stories.summary: While digging a trench at The Great Tythe Barn, workers stumbled upon five suspected World War II bombs, initially mistaking them for broken pipes. As their metal fins became visible, emergency services swiftly evacuated the area, setting up a 200-metre exclusion zone for safety. Identified as German explosives, the bombs were eventually neutralized in a controlled detonation, underscoring the historic shadows that still linger in various regions of Britain.

stories.title: MrBeast Funds Free School Lunches: Kansas teacher’s campaign sparks gift; families get relief
stories.summary: At Tonganoxie Middle School, agriculture teacher Beth Schartz took significant steps to address student lunch debt after a concerning incident involving unpaid lunch balances impacted a child. In a remarkable turn of events, YouTube sensation MrBeast stepped in, generously funding free lunches for the entire academic year. This initiative not only provided nourishing meals but also included free back-to-school clothing, positively impacting families and promoting inclusiveness in the school community.

stories.title: Trump jokes he'll move to Israel and become PM if Americans get 'tired' of him
stories.summary: In a lighthearted moment during a Fox News interview, Donald Trump playfully proposed his candidacy for the position of Israel's prime minister, citing a staggering 99 percent approval rating among Israelis. He went on to declare that by 2026, the US would cease its annual aid of $4 billion to Israel, sparking considerable debate over the implications for military support and relations, coinciding with the midterm elections unfolding in America.

stories.title: BJP, allies slam Neha Bora for 'anti-Hindu' remarks
stories.summary: Neha Bora of AISA has come under fire for her remarks about the Brahmanical system and temple safety. Her comments have been interpreted as reinforcing claims of anti-Hindu sentiments within Rahul Gandhi's ecosystem. BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia condemned her statements, accusing her of insulting priests and promoting divisive rhetoric. LJP chief Chirag Paswan urged Congress to reconsider its association with her and similar figures.

stories.title: Pennsylvania woman treated for breast cancer had rare lymphoma; court allows family's lawsuit
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania woman received breast cancer treatment for 13 months before doctors discovered she had a rare and aggressive lymphoma. She died in January 2019, and her family sued the treating oncologist, alleging that the delayed diagnosis reduced her chances of survival. After a trial court dismissed the case, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that a jury should hear the malpractice claim.

stories.title: Judge needn't face strictures for typos in judgement: SC
stories.summary: In a significant move, the Supreme Court intervened to address remarks made by the Rajasthan high court about a trial judge. This action stemmed from minor errors in a ruling, which the High Court harshly criticized, despite the fact that these did not alter the outcome of the case.

stories.title: Trump’s DOJ deploys 1,000 monitors across 50 states; Democrats allege voter intimidation
Encouraged by response to defence of SIR, BJP plans next political push
stories.summary: The BJP is concluding its initial campaign phase to promote the SIR initiative. Union home minister Amit Shah has reached out to Congress, proposing a parliamentary discussion on the topic. Their strategy focuses on addressing the opposition's criticism related to the SIR and electoral setbacks. A BJP-commissioned survey reveals substantial public backing for the initiative, with the next campaign phase due to launch after Diwali celebrations.

stories.title: ‘We will find you, hunt you down’: Trump’s DHS secretary warns illegal voters on Election Day; Newsom fights it out with ICE
SC to define right to privacy of protesters in public places
Who protects those counting America's votes? US election workers face threats amid midterms
stories.summary: In response to escalating threats and harassment, local government workers overseeing elections in the US are now under heightened security measures. This includes installation of bulletproof glass and emergency panic buttons, alongside training to manage aggressive behavior and suspicious items. The situation is compounded by the departure of numerous election officials, complicating recruitment efforts. Federal authorities remain dedicated to investigating threats to maintain the integrity of the electoral process.

Arkansas man loses tax offset bid as court upholds ex-wife's $183,000 business share
stories.summary: Following their divorce in 2017, a couple in Arkansas found themselves embroiled in a lengthy legal dispute concerning their jointly owned business, Groundskeeper. Conflicts emerged regarding the business's valuation and tax obligations. The Arkansas Court of Appeals confirmed the wife's claim of $183,000, inclusive of prejudgment interest from the divorce date, mandating Craig Ballegeer to acquire his former wife's half-interest in the business.

stories.summary: In a remarkable initiative, the Charles Antetokounmpo Family Foundation and Enaleia have repurposed discarded fishing gear into vibrant basketball nets, enhancing public courts across Athens. This project not only replaces damaged nets but also tackles marine pollution by transforming waste into valuable resources for the community. Young athletes can engage with these recycled nets, fostering a sense of environmental awareness alongside their love for sports.

stories.summary: Listed at $2 million, the unique Esperanza House embodies 138 years of history as a Queen Anne Victorian masterpiece with a bold purple exterior. Previously owned by Leonora Pierotti Thomas, the house is rich in artistic character yet demands extensive restoration. Nonetheless, essential features like the pool remain functional, and the agent appeals to buyers keen on its historic value and future possibilities.

stories.summary: With the 2026 midterm elections approaching, generative artificial intelligence is finding its way into the political arena. This technology creates highly convincing fake materials, which blur the lines between fact and fiction for voters. Campaigns utilize machine-learning tools to personalize outreach, raising concerns about trust in media integrity and the electoral process. Research shows that many voters fear how AI-generated content may undermine the fairness of elections.

stories.summary: Talon Assets, LLC acquired land in Atlanta for $220,000 at a county tax sale. Doubts about the property led them to request a refund and tax deed cancellation. However, Fulton County dismissed their case, invoking sovereign immunity as a legal defense. The Georgia Court of Appeals upheld this dismissal, leaving Talon's issues unresolved. This ruling highlights the challenges in pursuing financial claims against county governments in Georgia.

stories.title: Texas farmers turn 640 acres of donated land into college scholarships for 300 students
stories.summary: A 640-acre farmland donation made to a Texas school district in 1984 has become a source of college scholarships for hundreds of students. Local farmers in Gruver volunteer their labour and equipment to grow crops, generating approximately $400,000 annually. Since 2016, the initiative has distributed nearly $3 million to around 300 students, helping them pursue higher education.

Unveiled on November 1, this stupa strengthens the enduring friendship and cultural ties between India and Bhutan. This initiative highlights Bhutan's commitment to boosting its Buddhist identity and serves as a token of gratitude for India's continuous support in its developmental journey.

stories.title: One move, two gains: NHAI to desilt Bihar rivers and build roads with excavated material
stories.summary: Bihar's government has signed an agreement with the road transport ministry for river desilting to reduce flooding. The excavated silt and sand will be utilized in highway construction projects across the state. This initiative aims to improve water flow in rivers while providing construction materials at no cost. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary emphasized the impact of flooding on the state's agriculture and infrastructure.

The court clarified that accusations of inflated billing require concrete evidence, particularly following Flux Drive Inc.'s unsuccessful trade-secrets lawsuit. This ruling reinforces the notion that simply employing AI does not warrant a reduction in legal fees, establishing a significant precedent for similar cases moving forward.

stories.summary: As election day for the US midterms arrives, the atmosphere is charged with anticipation. Three distinct scenarios could shape the future of Congress: a sweeping Democratic wave may bring notable victories, whereas a slim Democratic majority may present hurdles in legislation. On the flip side, Republicans retaining control over both chambers could steer Trump's political agenda. The results await, holding the potential to influence the nation significantly.

Researchers discovered that vertically striped sheets recorded 2.8 times fewer bird collisions than plain sheets, while black sheets performed better than white ones. The findings could help make coastal buildings, ships and offshore facilities safer for seabirds.

stories.title: Trump unveils repaired Lincoln Memorial pool after costs exceed $14m, up from under $2m
stories.summary: The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has recently undergone extensive repairs, as unveiled by Trump, marking a significant and costly restoration effort. Budget overruns have pushed expenses to over $14 million, primarily due to algae problems stemming from a failed blue coating. Officials assert that these costs are essential for the pool's lasting quality. Fortunately, after the essential maintenance work, the site is now welcoming visitors once again.

stories.title: Ann Widdecombe’s Dartmoor home where she was murdered goes on sale for £900,000, 4 months after death
stories.summary: Ann Widdecombe’s Dartmoor home, where the former Conservative MP was murdered in July 2026, has been put on the market for £900,000, just four months after her death. The five-bedroom property, which she purchased for £600,000 in 2008, features a swimming pool, stables and extensive gardens, with its asking price reflecting a 50% increase.

The Washington Court of Appeals upheld rulings favouring both neighbours, including an order to remove a fence encroaching on one neighbour's land. The court also upheld legal-fee awards and granted the neighbours additional fees for the appeal.

stories.title: Meet Eva Outram, UK woman who quit her $58,000 NHS job; now lives in a caravan and saves $3,200 a month
stories.summary: After her impactful experience on 'Alone', Eva Outram, formerly an NHS project manager, swapped her city life for a caravan with her partner, Tom Park, focusing on simplicity and financial freedom. By working on farms for accommodation, they manage to save about $3,200 every month. Outram envisions creating outdoor skill workshops to foster nature appreciation and has plans to eventually buy land to construct their own residence.

stories.summary: Quincy Jones departed from this world in November 2024, but his legacy thrived, bringing in substantial revenue well into 2026. Much of this financial success stemmed from a remarkable $150 million deal for his extensive music catalog. Additionally, his enduring relationship with Michael Jackson fueled renewed interest following a blockbuster biopic's release.

stories.title: 132-year-old Kirby home reduced to rubble
stories.summary: Houston's historic Kirby Mansion, a Tudor Revival gem, was abruptly leveled after city inspectors stopped renovation efforts over permit issues. Despite being well-maintained, the new owner proceeded with the demolition unauthorized, leading to outcry from preservationists. The community mourned the mansion with a vigil, pressing for policy reforms and alluding to a gas station development that might replace the beloved site.

stories.title: Dhirendra Shastri apologises for 'your Krishna, our Ram' remark; controversy explained
stories.summary: In a video message posted on social media from Kenya's Nairobi, Shastri on Monday said he had no intention of insulting any deity or suggesting that one was superior to the other. He apologised to anyone whose religious sentiments may have been hurt by his comments. The controversy began during a recent Ram Katha in Karera in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district.

Controversy erupted when the Samajwadi Party dissociated itself from remarks made by AISA leader Neha Bora concerning caste matters.

stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has extended a challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for an open debate on several allegations. Rahul gandhi further suggested that the debate take place in the presence of media and youth, proposing Mohan Bhagwat as a moderator.

Police detained several protesters, including Bora, as restrictions on public gatherings were imposed in parts of the capital.

stories.title: Bhutan's glacial lake outburst exposes growing disaster threat across the Himalayas
stories.summary: Bhutan experienced a significant glacial lake outburst that raised concerns regarding devastating glacial floods in the Himalayas. Authorities are monitoring a temporary lake created by debris from the initial flood event. The risks posed by melting glaciers are increasingly threatening both infrastructure and communities across the region. India, sharing river systems with Bhutan, has started its own review of disaster preparedness plans.

Ex-Air chief AP Singh wrote to Rajnath, urged him to keep Race Course land under IAF control
US doctor reduces work hours to care for baby, court upholds higher income assessment
stories.summary: An Indiana doctor who reduced her working hours to care for her newborn daughter has lost her appeal after a court calculated her weekly earning capacity at $8,811, despite her reported income of $6,677. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld the decision, finding that she was capable of working full-time. It also upheld an order allowing her former husband three overnight stays a week with their daughter.

stories.title: 'Huge impact on polls': IB opposes shifting convict in ex-Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassination to state jail
stories.summary: The Intelligence Bureau has raised concerns regarding Jagtar Singh Hawara's potential transfer from Tihar Jail to a prison in Punjab, citing possible ramifications for the impending assembly elections. Hawara, who is serving a sentence for the assassination of Beant Singh and is considered a high-risk individual, could see his transfer postponed according to his attorney.

'Gaddar': BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of treason, calls him 'Bhasmasur'
stories.summary: BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused Rahul Gandhi of treason and promoting anarchy in India's democracy. He raised questions about Gandhi's foreign engagements and the Congress's MoU with the Communist Party of China. Allegations included inappropriate conduct towards a woman police officer during protests against the Chief Election Commissioner. Bhatia warned the opposition leaders about the potential backlash from the public regarding their calls for regime change.

stories.title: In 1610, one astronomer challenged Galileo’s discovery; their books survived together for centuries
stories.summary: In 1610, the revolutionary work of Galileo Galilei, titled Sidereus Nuncius, brought to light the moons orbiting Jupiter, challenging the traditional view of astronomy. This groundbreaking revelation incited controversy, notably with Francesco Sizzi, who dismissed these lunar discoveries as mere optical deceptions. Recently, a rare edition of Galileo's masterpiece fetched an astonishing Rs 2.07 crore, underscoring the enduring impact of his innovations amidst the scientific skepticism of his era.

stories.title: Meet Diana Anderson: 57-year-old woman charged after dozens of keepsakes allegedly stolen from graves of loved ones in Canada; 20 families report missing items
stories.summary: A troubling situation has emerged at Milton Evergreen Cemetery in Ontario, where numerous families have reported stolen items from gravesites. Following an inquiry, a 57-year-old woman has been arrested in connection with these thefts. Police have managed to recover sentimental objects, such as lanterns and plants, and are actively contacting families who may still be unaware of the losses. As the investigation broadens, additional charges against the suspect are likely.

stories.title: 'We're out of time': Florida pilot's chilling last words before jet plunged to ground
stories.summary: A Learjet 60 tragically crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, resulting in the deaths of nine individuals aboard. The pilot made urgent distress calls while reporting severe icing and turbulence shortly before the crash occurred. Descent rates reached alarming levels, culminating in a drop of up to 22,000 feet per minute. Investigations by the National Transportation Safety Board are focusing on weather conditions and possible structural failure.

India, Israel vote against Pakistan-backed UN arms control resolution: What it means
stories.summary: In a significant move, India and Israel opposed a UN resolution proposed by Pakistan and Belarus concerning regional arms control. Despite its adoption with strong backing, both nations voiced serious reservations. India's delegate argued that national security transcends geographic lines, highlighting the potential distraction from established UN disarmament agreements. Additionally, India expressed concerns regarding specific references to South Asian arms control measures present in the resolution.

stories.summary: A 26-year-old Australian fisherman, Matthew Maurice, won A$1 million after catching an 80cm red-tagged barramundi during a fishing trip with his younger brother in the Northern Territory. The Thursday catch made him only the second person to win the top prize in the Million Dollar Fish competition's 12-year history. Maurice plans to use the money to buy a house and clear outstanding payments.

stories.title: Ohio jail inmates’ portraits help 18 shelter dogs find forever homes
stories.summary: Inmates at the Franklin County Corrections Center have been drawing portraits of shelter dogs. Their artwork has resulted in higher adoption rates, helping many dogs find homes. This initiative allows inmates to contribute positively to the community while creating a connection with potential adopters. The portraits humanize the dogs, making them more relatable to visitors. Such simple actions have led to transformative impacts for both dogs and incarcerated individuals.
