stories.summary: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has embarked on an innovative project to leverage materials from Bihar's rivers for highway development, aiming to alleviate flooding. This strategic move, a result of a memorandum of understanding between the Bihar government and the Ministry of Road Transport, is designed to tackle the dual flooding challenges posed by local rainfall and external water influx.

stories.title: Dilip Ghosh takes 'Sonia' jibe at Mamata for joining INDIA bloc rally against SIR
stories.summary: Dilip Ghosh has publicly lambasted Mamata Banerjee for her involvement in the INDIA bloc rally concerning changes to the electoral roll. He argues her party's diminishing political clout is prompting her to seek validation through an alliance with Congress. Ghosh highlighted her past victories, labeling her claims regarding electoral integrity as hypocritical, and pointed out the positive impact of removing fraudulent voters in fostering fair elections in West Bengal.

stories.title: 'Targeting civilian infrastructure must end': MEA after Indian national killed in attack on ship in Oman
'Rs 25cr spent on ads to claim no stubble burning, FIRs tell another story': BJP targets AAP govt in Punjab
stories.summary: Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa accused the Punjab government of permitting stubble burning while contradicting its claims. He alleged that Punjab's government had registered FIRs against farmers involved in stubble burning activities. Sirsa criticized the appointment of Reena Gupta as chairperson of the Punjab Pollution Control Board as an attempt to manipulate pollution data. He emphasized the adverse impact of Punjab's stubble burning on Delhi's air quality.

stories.title: California judge orders one former partner to pay the other $66,192 in legal fees after house dispute
stories.summary: Matthew Shroder and Mackenzie Fotsch are currently embroiled in legal disputes regarding a jointly owned property in Sausalito. After achieving a partial victory in a motion to strike, Shroder sought $90,010 in attorney fees and the court awarded him $66,192.50. This amount includes $40,887.50 for anti-SLAPP proceedings and $21,700 for the fee application, yet does not resolve their ongoing property conflict.

stories.title: Meet Hazmatt: Oklahoma’s 20-foot reclining robot made from discarded dumpsters, built for just over $14,000
stories.summary: Norman, Oklahoma has unveiled a captivating new public sculpture named Hazmatt, crafted from recycled dumpsters. This striking giant robot, funded by surplus construction funds totaling slightly over $14,000, is strategically located at the city’s Household Hazardous Waste Facility. Hazmatt serves to inspire the community, highlighting the importance of responsible waste management and showcasing the potential for creative reuse of discarded materials.

stories.title: Reddit Fights Teen Account Ban: Platforms contest Australia’s under-16 law; ruling may sway global curbs
stories.summary: In late 2025, Australia enacted a law prohibiting individuals under 16 from accessing social media. However, Reddit and a libertarian organization are contesting this legislation in the High Court. While the law seeks to safeguard youth, it faces backlash for its lacking effectiveness, as many teenagers under this age still manage to go online. The government has responded by imposing stricter penalties on non-compliant social media platforms.

stories.title: Judge Judy’s mentoring programme marks 20 years, reaching 1,500 young women
stories.summary: Her Honor Mentoring began with a modest gathering of girls two decades ago and has since flourished remarkably. This program matches high school seniors with dedicated mentors, guiding them through educational and career paths. Participants acquire vital skills, including financial literacy, that prepare them for both college and professional futures while fostering nurturing relationships that empower young women to chase their dreams.

stories.title: 'Doesn’t have courage to call all-party meet?’: Congress questions Shah over delay in discussion on delimitation Bill
Wisconsin father-son dealership feud ends with $321,330 civil-theft damages against son
stories.summary: A serious conflict arose between Carl Schneider and his son Chris regarding Hybrid Car Store Inc., their family-run dealership. Chris misappropriated corporate funds to pay off personal obligations, resulting in significant financial repercussions. The situation escalated with multiple lawsuits, resulting in a federal court ruling that held Chris accountable for civil theft.

stories.title: 1 killed, 13 rescued after unidentified aerial object strikes Indian vessel near Oman
stories.summary: An Indian seafarer from Gujarat was killed after an unidentified aerial object struck the Indian-flagged vessel MSV AL JUSUFI off the Oman coast on Monday. The remaining 13 crew members were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard. Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal said Indian authorities were coordinating with Oman to assist the survivors and arrange their repatriation.

stories.title: Man claims Crown land linked to Napoleon’s former dairy after 15 years
Record 2026 Campaign Spending: Billionaires, crypto fuel $11.9bn US midterms; TV ads dominate
stories.summary: The 2026 midterm elections in the U.S. are on track to raise a staggering $12 billion, marking the most expensive campaign in history. Wealthy individuals and corporations wield increasing influence over financing, with billionaire Elon Musk standing out as the top donor, having contributed nearly $500 million to Republican candidates.

stories.title: Can Trump defy history? The big battles shaping US midterms
SAD MP Harsimrat Badal writes to Om Birla over farmer's body removal, seeks action against SSP
stories.summary: Harsimrat Kaur Badal has reached out to the Lok Sabha Speaker to demand accountability from Mansa SSP Vaibhav Chaudhary. She accuses the police of inappropriately removing a farmer's body during a protest against alleged drug trade connections. Badal mentions intimidation tactics used by the police and claims her concerns were met with dismissal by the SSP.

stories.title: Maldives' former foreign minister Abdulla Shahid arrested in child abuse case
Netanyahu open to 'broad' government formation after election setback but rules out Arab parties
stories.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu has expressed a readiness to establish a broad coalition government under his guidance. His Likud party is attempting to stall the certification process of the recent election results, citing claims of foreign interference. Netanyahu has dismissed the option of collaborating with Arab parties, due to accusations of terrorism against them.

stories.title: Judge Clears Capitol Event: US court backs Satanic Temple’s free speech claim; Iowa plans appeal
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a federal judge has mandated that Iowa officials allow the local chapter of the Satanic Temple to hold its holiday event. This decision comes after multiple rejections linked to building regulations. Despite state officials' reservations about the event, the judge found their concerns unconvincing. Activities scheduled include caroling and crafts for children. However, state officials are prepared to contest the ruling's validity.

stories.title: 26 killed as Russia strikes Ukraine school used for aid distribution
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a school being used as a humanitarian aid distribution centre in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing at least 26 people, with around 20 others missing. Rescue efforts were disrupted by fresh drone attacks. Meanwhile, cyberattacks triggered fake emergency alerts in Ukraine and Russia, as a limited ceasefire in the Kherson region expired.

stories.title: E-sign for SIR tribunal judges soon, can upload bulk orders on portal
For 'outstanding vision', Bhutan dedicates one of 108 stupas to PM Modi
Marital discord no ground for termination of pregnancy: SC
Investment in renewable energy cushioned Iran war blow: PM Modi
First in 47 years: No operational fatality in CRPF in an entire year
Unhappy with Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, six NCP biggies meet Amit Shah
Mammal Reintroductions At Sturt: six native species return; project expands beyond fences
stories.summary: Ecologists Rebecca West and Reece Pedler are leading an inspiring initiative called the Wild Deserts project in New South Wales, focused on reviving native mammal populations that have been absent for over a century. Their efforts have successfully seen the reintroduction of multiple species to Sturt National Park, where they are now thriving and breeding in the wild.

stories.title: Murtho Habitat Restoration: Former vineyard revived for regent parrots; family project spans generations
stories.summary: After departing from the wine industry, Tony and Cherie Townsend embarked on a remarkable project to repurpose their 40-acre vineyard into a sanctuary for regent parrots. Their family and local volunteers, spanning four generations, are actively involved in this conservation initiative. Backed by the Murraylands and Riverland Landscape Board, over 3,000 native seedlings have been planted, fostering vital habitats and illustrating the crucial role private land plays in enhancing biodiversity.

stories.title: 'Air fares up by 700%': Don't fly, says SC
SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green
SC orders trial in Ram temple donation case; SIT says Rs 2.7 crore stolen
Day after quitting as Punjab MLAs, 3 AAP rebels come into BJP fold
Nebraska court vacates sale of couple's home over husband's commercial lease debt
stories.summary: A couple in Nebraska was on the brink of losing their family home due to a commercial lease debt solely tied to the husband. The creditor aimed to sell the property to reclaim funds. The Nebraska Supreme Court stepped in, clarifying that the lower court misapplied the judgment lien, which only affected the husband's interest.

stories.title: Record Subsurface Warming In Monterey Bay: MBARI logs 18.18°C at 60m; tropical species move north
stories.summary: Scientists have announced that temperatures at 200 feet off Monterey Bay have reached their highest levels in nearly forty years. This rise is attributed to the forthcoming 2026-27 El Niño, with sightings of tropical species migrating northward, suggesting significant ecological transformations. These shifts in ocean conditions pose a risk to deep-sea food availability, impacting various marine ecosystems.

stories.title: Bangka Slow Loris Rediscovered: Rescues reveal more than 90 venomous primates; habitat loss still threatens
stories.summary: A groundbreaking study reveals the comeback of the Bangka slow loris, once feared lost or critically endangered. Over 90 individuals have been documented on Bangka Island from 2015 to 2025, shedding light on their survival. Wildlife rescues have been instrumental not only in recording their existence but also in aiding rehabilitation efforts.

stories.title: Navy rescues 20 crew members of fishing vessel from armed pirates over 3,000km from Mumbai, Rajnath praises 48-hr op
Atlanta landlord's $50,000 fundraiser grows into $16.5 million, helping 5,500 families avoid eviction
stories.summary: Jason Dozier initiated a fundraising campaign in 2020, which led to the creation of the Housing Stability Fund. This programme has provided financial assistance to over 5,500 families facing housing insecurity in the Atlanta area. By streamlining processes and collaborating with landlords, the programme aims to prevent evictions and court backlogs. Follow-up surveys indicate that a majority of recipients remain in stable housing a year later.

stories.title: Louisiana woman wins nearly $450,000 after $32,500 river barrier fails and home shifts
stories.summary: After suffering extensive structural damage to her home from a failing wooden bulkhead, Elizabeth Molbert took legal action against the contractor involved and succeeded. The jury assigned 75% of the blame to the contractor and, in a twist, the appeals court ruled that Molbert had no fault in the matter, increasing her compensation to $448,431.34 and adjusting her mental anguish damages to align with her financial difficulties.

stories.title: Row erupts after Scottish govt sends IT contract to Bengaluru to administer welfare payment
Texas opens 3,000-acre state park along the Colorado River with $1 billion expansion fund
stories.summary: Post Oak Ridge has officially opened, marking Texas' latest state park. Spanning over 3,000 acres, it features two hiking trails along four miles of scenic routes. Plans for future camping facilities and river access are on track for completion by 2029. Input from the community has been vital in guiding the park's development, as part of a larger effort to expand public outdoor spaces across Texas.

stories.title: Howard Stern's wife Beth turns grief into rescue mission, helping over 2,000 cats find homes
stories.summary: After the heartbreaking passing of their bulldog, Howard and Beth Stern channeled their sorrow into meaningful change by founding Bianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center, part of North Shore Animal League America. This center improves the conditions for cats waiting for adoption and boosts rescue capabilities. With over 2,000 cats fostered since 2013, Beth's dedicated efforts have played a crucial role in spotlighting the importance of adopting shelter animals nationwide.

stories.title: Farm Becomes Wildlife Retreat: Olivia Newton-John reshaped Dalwood estate; sale tied to cancer work
stories.summary: Olivia Newton-John owned a country estate in Australia that she transformed over nearly four decades. This property included natural features and a significant amount of wildlife habitat that she developed. After battling cancer, the estate was sold in 2019 for $4.6 million, reflecting changes in her priorities. Newton-John's connection to the area continued through her involvement with a wellness retreat she co-founded.

stories.title: Rahul can be PM only in mock Parliament: Amit Shah
Stephen Curry-backed golf teams make history with women's first NEC title and men's third win
stories.summary: Howard University's golf program reached new heights when both men's and women's teams won their conference championships. The women's team claimed its first-ever Northeast Conference title in April 2026. Just days later, the men's team secured its third consecutive NEC championship victory. The successes highlighted the growth of the program, supported by NBA star Stephen Curry's funding.

stories.title: Days after Farooq’s Pak praise, Mehbooba says Abdullahs created distrust between Kashmir & rest of India
Nebraska court rejects handwritten will signed by man but written largely by his longtime partner
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, Nebraska's Supreme Court declared a handwritten will invalid, stating that the primary handwriting was not that of the testator. The court reaffirmed the original 1984 will, which allocated assets to the deceased's sons. This decision underlined the necessity for a holographic will to be solely in the writer's hand to clarify testamentary intent, especially amid disputes from a long-term partner after Douglas G. Todd's death.

stories.title: Maryland court orders new trial over $3.2 million trust after sisters challenge inheritance
stories.summary: A Maryland appeals court has mandated a new trial concerning a $3.2 million trust fund held by three sisters. The court identified procedural errors that prevented two sisters from presenting crucial handwriting evidence regarding the trust. Their claims included accusations of undue influence exerted by their sister, the main beneficiary. The appeals court emphasized issues with the previous trial's allowed testimonies and evidence exclusions.

stories.title: North Carolina sculptor's tiny cabin grew into a 60-foot woodland castle
Paul McCartney-backed Liverpool arts institute celebrates 400+ graduates 30 years on
stories.summary: The LIPA held its 2026 graduation ceremony celebrating its 30th anniversary by awarding degrees to its very first graduates. With over 400 students from 28 different countries in attendance, this event marked a monumental occasion. Sir Paul McCartney was on hand to honor five notable figures for their artistry and impact on the cultural landscape, showcasing LIPA's commitment to nurturing creative talent across various fields, including music, theatre, and film.

stories.title: Fake nuclear threat alert sent to Ukrainians after emergency app hacked
IISc develops 3D-printed model to study how cancer drugs penetrate tumours
RLD leader projects Jayant Chaudhary as NDA's face for 2027 UP polls
Homebuyers body urges PM to recast RERA; separate promotion from protection
ICE officer surrenders after grand jury indicts him for running over immigrant with vehicle in Texas
Trump admin asks Supreme Court to set aside 20,000 California ballots over citizenship row a day before midterms
Power outage hits Washington DC's Foggy Bottom, over 1,100 Pepco customers affected
Indian Sikh couple's New Zealand asylum claim rejected after NZ$336,000 crore debt dispute with Punjab moneylender
Entire police force resigns in Georgia city; Mayor Craig Timmons admits tracking police chief's truck
stories.summary: A small Georgia city is facing a police staffing crisis after its entire full-time police force resigned. Mayor Craig Timmons admitted placing a GPS tracker on Police Chief Lamar Bunn's truck over concerns about his timesheets. Bunn has denied wrongdoing, while the mass resignations have left the city relying on the county sheriff's office for police coverage.

stories.title: Historic Mansion Sale Soars: Nantucket’s Hadwen-Wright House fetches $15.25 million; hidden cistern preserved
stories.summary: The Hadwen-Wright House in Nantucket fetched an impressive $15.25 million, after being originally listed at $15.5 million. This stunning mansion, a prime example of Greek Revival architecture, is steeped in history. Its extensive renovations not only maintained original features but also unveiled a unique brick-lined cistern now preserved for guests. This sale highlights the lasting appeal of Nantucket's historically significant residences.

stories.title: First in 47 years: CRPF completes 12 months without any operational casualties
stories.summary: CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated personnel on the milestone, saying the last operational death in the force was recorded on October 30, 2025. The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979. The milestone comes against the backdrop of another serious challenge facing the force, the rising number of personnel dying by suicide.

stories.title: 'NCP united under Sunetra Pawar': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
stories.summary: The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".

stories.title: 'Surge in popularity after reality show': Tej Pratap Yadav asks for enhanced security from Centre
stories.summary: In a post on X, Yadav said his recent appearance on a reality show had increased his popularity, with large numbers of people approaching him in public places to take photographs. He said the crowds posed a risk not only to him but also to the lone security personnel currently assigned to him.

stories.title: Cyclone Murusu: 19 flights cancelled, NDRF on standby as coastal states brace for severe storm - top development
Cyclone Murasu to make landfall near at Andhra coast tonight; 120 kmph winds expected
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu has intensified and is predicted to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast soon. It is expected to bring strong winds reaching up to 120 kmph and heavy rainfall. Several districts in Andhra Pradesh will experience severe weather conditions due to the cyclone. Precautionary measures have been implemented, including rescue operations and evacuation arrangements. Fishermen have been advised to avoid venturing into the sea during this period.

stories.title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav's recent visit to Azam Khan in jail underscores their deep political connection amidst ongoing legal troubles. Following Azam's fleeting bail, the Enforcement Directorate swiftly took him back into custody, adding complexity to the Samajwadi Party's election preparations. Balancing support for Azam while appealing to Muslim constituents presents a significant challenge for Akhilesh as he navigates potential electoral repercussions.

stories.title: 'Your social media posts amounted to instigation': Bombay HC pulls up actor Imran Khan - top quotes
stories.summary: A bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna remarked that instead of deporting Khan immediately, authorities had shown leniency by issuing him a notice asking him to leave the country. Khan's lawyer, Venkatesh Dhond, responded by submitting an undertaking that the 43-year-old actor would not participate in any protest in the future. He also conveyed Khan's unconditional apology to the court.

stories.title: 'Rahul Gandhi has no vision, will be responsible for Congress's wipeout': BJP's Nitin Nabin at anti-SIR march
'3 crore Bangladeshi infiltrators don't exist on voters' list': Amit Shah counters Rahul's anti-SIR pitch
stories.summary: In a verbal blitzkrieg, a day after Rahul's mega Ramlila Maidan rally in the national capital, Shah said that behind the Congress's criticism of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) lies an "attempt to protect illegal Bangladeshi infiltrators", three crore of whom, he claimed, were struck off the electoral rolls during the revision.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Imran Khan apologises to Bombay HC, SC allows green crackers & more
'You became PM because of foreign help': Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi for debate
61 detained in Ahmedabad as crackdown on illegal Bangladeshi immigrants intensifies
stories.summary: Ahmedabad's Crime Branch has taken action against 61 suspected illegal immigrants, mostly hailing from Bangladesh, in a city-wide effort to bolster safety ahead of Diwali. The police executed synchronized raids across different localities to pinpoint foreign nationals living without legal status. Deportation processes are currently being initiated, furthering previous measures aimed at curbing illegal immigration from Bangladesh.

stories.title: Centre notifies grievance redressal rules under VB-G RAM G Act, sets 15-day resolution deadline
stories.summary: The Centre has officially introduced grievance redressal protocols as per the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. Complaints must receive resolution within 15 days, with preliminary inquiries to be conducted in seven working days. Individuals can lodge grievances through various methods, ensuring that all complaints will be recorded. Complainants will have the opportunity to present their cases, and issues that remain unresolved shall be escalated for further scrutiny and resolution.

stories.title: California accountant gets 63 months in prison after $8.2 million backyard homes fraud
stories.summary: A California accountant has been sentenced to 63 months in prison for defrauding investors of more than $8.2 million through fake real estate projects. Ethan Joseph Sanchez promised to use their money to build backyard homes but instead lost it through risky day trading. A federal judge also ordered him to forfeit over $8.2 million and pay restitution to victims.

stories.title: Texas farmer earns $200,000 yearly by leasing 600 acres for solar panels
Discarded racing tyres transformed into 17-foot sculpture at Ohio park; artist Chakaia Booker unveils ‘Transit’
stories.summary: Chakaia Booker recently unveiled her stunning 17-foot sculpture named 'Transit' at Lock 3 park in Akron, Ohio. Crafted from recycled Goodyear Eagle F1 racing tyres, the piece pays homage to the city's rubber industry legacy. Composed of two elegantly curved forms supported by stainless steel, this installation, initiated in 2023, emphasizes the importance of contemporary public art created by female artists.

stories.title: Titanic passenger wrote to friend before fatal voyage, letter fetches $16,100 at auction
stories.summary: A letter written by Titanic passenger George Graham on April 10, 1912, shortly before the ship left Southampton, revealed his hope of meeting a business colleague in Berlin the following year. Graham died when the Titanic sank five days later. The letter survived and was eventually sold for $16,100 at an auction in New York, setting a world record.

stories.title: Imran Khan tenders unconditional apology in HC over anti-SIR protest participation
Storm Triggers La Palma Blackout: power outage hits island amid heavy rain; PLATECA plan activated
stories.summary: On Monday, a powerful storm wreaked havoc on La Palma, Spain, causing widespread electricity disruptions. The local government reported rainfall intensities hitting 30 litres per square metre per hour. In urgent response, officials issued a top-tier rainfall alert starting at midnight. The PLATECA emergency plan was activated to ensure the management of public services. Meanwhile, snowfall blanketed neighboring Tenerife over the weekend.

stories.title: Virginia couple's dream garden sparks dispute over backyard land
Halloween turns deadly across US as gun violence leaves at least 24 dead, 94 injured
FPCE writes to PM Modi, lists 5 key changes to RERA to strengthen homebuyer protection
South Korean lawmaker denied US visa for 1991 conviction. Three days later, he was issued A-2 visa after Marco Rubio's diplomatic intervention
SC allows green crackers in Delhi-NCR for Diwali, full ban from November 9
US midterms 2026: Trump calls Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a ‘jihadist’ at Iowa rally, hails Republican Mike Rogers as 'apple pie'
Sonia Gandhi meets Lalu Yadav in Delhi; Tejashwi shares photos, reminisces UPA-era tie
stories.summary: Tejashwi Yadav, Bihar leader of the opposition, said Sonia Gandhi had personally expressed a desire to meet his father after learning that he was in Delhi for a medical check-up. He also pointed out that the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's government had allocated more than Rs 1.45 lakh crore for Bihar's development.

stories.title: Indiana father moves to Virginia for new job, court upholds ex-wife's custody of son
stories.summary: An Indiana father who lost his $350,000-a-year job after 26 years and moved to Virginia for work has lost his appeal in a custody dispute. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld a decision granting his ex-wife sole legal custody and primary physical custody of their son. It also ordered him to pay $4,000 towards her legal fees, citing the income difference between the parents.

stories.title: US midterm elections 2026: What they are, why they matter and when results will be out
stories.summary: The US midterm elections are set for November 3, affecting Congress and local offices. Voters will select members of the House and Senate, impacting legislative control. Republican majorities currently hold both chambers, with Democrats needing net gains to gain control. Key issues influencing voter decisions include inflation, immigration, and administration performance. Election results will be determined by state officials and may lead to contested outcomes in closely fought races.

stories.title: 'Don't travel by air. Next case': SC judge on plea alleging 700% airfare hike
Kentucky landowner loses $800,000 riverfront land appeal after skipping floodplain variance process
stories.summary: A Kentucky landowner faced a setback as the state's Court of Appeals upheld a dismissal of his compensation claim related to floodplain regulations. Since he did not apply for necessary variances or receive final decisions on development, the court's affirmation of the lower court's ruling complicates his plans. However, the ruling leaves room for potential future claims if proper administrative steps are taken.

stories.title: How a 13-year-old built a homemade pretzel business selling bags for $2
‘Rahul Gandhi fostering chaos’: BJP questions Congress over SIR row
Bulgaria elects Iliana Iotova as president, pro-Russia candidate defeats pro-Western rival
stories.summary: Iliana Iotova has triumphed in Bulgaria's presidential runoff, unseating the pro-western contender, Andrey Gyurov. Her campaign prioritized improving livelihoods, fostering peace, and confronting future challenges. This historic win makes Iotova the first female president elected directly by the Bulgarian populace. With security concerns heightened by recent drone attacks in the Black Sea, low voter turnout reflected the deep political rifts concerning Bulgaria's relationship with Russia.

stories.title: Kentucky woman challenges prenup over language difficulties, appeals court rejects her claim
stories.summary: A woman who moved from China to Kentucky on a fiance visa and signed a prenuptial agreement just 11 days after arriving in the US has lost her legal challenge following her divorce. Despite her husband's assets exceeding $1 million compared with her $39,000, the Kentucky Court of Appeals upheld the agreement, rejecting her claims of pressure and language difficulties.

stories.title: Meet Emily Herra, 17-year-old who turned a trash-filled lot into a community garden; won $10,000 for climate work
stories.summary: Co-founder of Veggie Nuggets, Emily Herra, collaborated with a team to revitalize an abandoned plot into a vibrant community garden. Despite facing setbacks, such as a contractor's destruction of their work, the group demonstrated resilience and rebuilt their garden. Their dedication earned them the Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes, which aids future climate activism. Herra's initiative spotlights the impactful role youth can play in fostering sustainability in their communities.

stories.title: 'Rahul camp insecure of Priyanka': BJP alleges rift between siblings, accuses leader of opposition of 'sidelining' sister
Lady Gaga and her mother built youth mental-health foundation; its programme has now crossed 100,000 certificates worldwide
stories.summary: Lady Gaga and her mother, Cynthia Germanotta, celebrated a remarkable achievement with the Born This Way Foundation as they announced that more than 100,000 individuals have successfully earned the Be There Certificate worldwide. This milestone, part of the Generation Be There campaign, emphasizes the foundation's commitment to promoting mental health awareness and education, enabling compassionate responses to those facing mental health challenges in their communities.

stories.title: Utah businessman mailed thousands of bricks, forcing the US to rewrite postal rules
Ayodhya Ram temple donation embezzlement case: Chargesheet filed, Supreme Court allows petitioners to assist trial
'Act responsibly': Taliban urges US over planned deportation of Afghan immigrants
California teen wins $10,000 for system that controls computers using tongue movements and blinks
stories.summary: Hollie Tang, a talented student from Wilson High School, has innovatively developed a system named Tonguage, designed to empower individuals with disabilities. This groundbreaking technology enables users to navigate devices through tongue movements and eye blinks. Winning the top scholarship at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair in Phoenix, Tang highlighted the potential of technology to enhance lives.

stories.title: Meet the three former AAP leaders who switched sides to join BJP ahead of Punjab polls
'Don't take court for granted': Delhi court summons actor Nora Fatehi again in Rs 200-crore extortion case
‘Youth-oppressive NDA govt’: Tejashwi accuses Nitish of toppling Mahagathbandhan regime in 2024
Big setback for AAP ahead of Punjab elections; 3 rebel MLAs join BJP
2 Congress workers held for hurling beer bottles at BJP headquarters in Kerala
stories.summary: In a heated political climate in Thiruvananthapuram, two Congress party workers were apprehended for allegedly hurling beer bottles at the BJP headquarters in Kerala. The situation escalated tensions between the rival parties. Following protests and demands from BJP for arrests, the police utilized CCTV footage for a thorough investigation, leading to the identification of the suspects as local Congress members involved in the incident.

stories.title: Punjab: AAP to seek cancellation of membership of 2 MLAs after they quit party
'2.5 lakh shops shut, Rs 10,000 crore loss': Delhi traders blame INDIA bloc rally for business disruption
INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan saw creative expression take centre stage as slogans, posters and placards delivered the message
stories.summary: In a momentous gathering, the INDIA bloc's supporters came together at Ramlila Maidan to address pressing political issues. Leaders from multiple parties spoke passionately about the necessity for change, particularly calling for the ousting of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This event highlighted the importance of unity against perceived electoral injustices, with speakers weaving in historical contexts to bolster their arguments regarding voting rights and electoral fairness.

stories.title: Kiren Rijiju jibes at Congress over INDIA bloc's Ramlila rally crowd photo, calls it 'AI-generated'
J&K: NC Srinagar MP Mehdi to quit party tomorrow to fight it back on 'ideological' turf
Fresh Iran strikes after US midterms? Inside Trump-Netanyahu's 'tough' call
stories.summary: Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a tough phone call regarding Iran and military strategies. They discussed the possibility of military action after the upcoming US midterm elections. Trump expressed readiness for diplomacy, while Netanyahu urged immediate strikes against Iran. Diplomatic initiatives continue, with the US Vice President sending a letter to Iran's national security chief.

stories.title: Desi Bullet Train closer to reality as squeeze test nears completion
6 Indian trekkers 'ignore weather warnings', get stranded in Nepal
SC upholds HC order allowing I-T to reassess income of ex-CJI's sons
Could Einstein’s equations explain the universe’s expansion?
stories.summary: Researchers from UC Davis have proposed that dark energy may not be necessary to explain the universe's acceleration. They found weak points in the Lambda-cold dark matter model using Einstein's equations. By examining instabilities in Friedmann spacetimes, they suggest alternative explanations for cosmic expansion. Their work raises questions about the Copernican principle in the context of current models. This research could lead to significant shifts in our understanding of cosmology.

stories.title: Scientists have developed a new technology that could make electric car batteries smaller, lighter and longer-lasting, potentially letting drivers travel farther on a single charge without carrying a heavier battery
stories.summary: Scientists from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology developed a new technology for anode-free batteries. This innovative approach focuses on enhancing lithium deposition to improve battery efficiency and longevity. By restructuring the copper surface for lithium storage, they have addressed issues with dendrite formation. Applying a thin layer of MXene further stabilizes the battery's performance.

stories.title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
Ranch Easement Preserves Habitat: Winn descendants shield 165 acres; Blanco River recharge gains
stories.summary: Four Winns Ranch in Texas, a treasured historical site, is preserved through dedicated efforts by the Winn family alongside conservation partners. Spanning 165 acres, this land is vital for protecting local wildlife habitats and water sources. Originally acquired by the noteworthy artist James Buchanan Buck Winn Jr., the ranch possesses rich cultural heritage while fostering agricultural and ecotourism activities, aiding the survival of rare birds and endangered aquatic species.

stories.title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
12th century Nepalese Manjushri statue sold for about Rs 166 crore in 2026
stories.summary: A 12th-century Manjushri sculpture from Nepal recently sold for around ₹166 crore, illuminating the exceptional artistry of Newar creators from the Kathmandu Valley. This sculpture's intriguing journey through different collections illustrates its cultural significance and uniqueness. Furthermore, the influence of Newar craftsmanship on Buddhist art permeated throughout Tibet and Asia, showcasing Nepal's profound artistic legacy and its vital role in international art history.

stories.title: 1984 survivors, Sikh groups question timing of INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, seek apology
Gyanesh has to go, PM & Shah next, says Rahul Gandhi at anti-CEC rally
12-year-old London boy raises £13,000 for wildlife, wins Attenborough's praise

The evidence hints at both a targeted attack and social care, as the skeleton bore previous injuries. This discovery serves as a window into the dualities of early human life, showcasing their capacity for both violence and compassion.

Hidden away in a drawer for more than 55 years by the family of the dealer, this remarkable figure was revealed as a warder, part of the legendary Lewis Chessmen collection. Originally found in 1831, this collection comprises 93 intricately carved pieces from 1150 to 1200 AD, though the auction leaves four original pieces still unaccounted for.

In 1913, an Ohio couple sent their eight-month-old son to his grandmother through the postal service

Ingenious parents even started shipping their small children to reduce travel expenses, gaining notoriety when six-year-old May Pierstorff was dispatched 73 miles away. This phenomenon sparked national debate, leading to the ban of child parceling, although similar incidents lingered until 1915, prompting stricter postal regulations to curb such extraordinary practices.

stories.title: Idaho Supreme Court revives condo owners' challenge to property changes approved by 88% vote
stories.summary: The Idaho Supreme Court has revived a legal dispute involving condominium owners challenging changes to property ownership. The contentious amendments were made by the Crystal Beach Condominium Association, affecting owners' shares and rental rules. A previous dismissal by a lower court has been partly overturned, confirming owners' rights to challenge changes impacting their property. Plaintiffs now have their claims for declaratory relief and title slander allowed to proceed.

stories.title: Texas court reopens insurance dispute after landslide destroys two homeowners' backyards
stories.summary: A legal dispute involving home insurance coverage in Travis County has been returned to court for further hearings. The Texas Third Court of Appeal overturned a previous ruling that held the insurer liable for damages. Homeowners claimed that earth movement caused significant damage to their properties, leading to a denial of their insurance claims. The appeals court requires the insurer to demonstrate the cause of the landslide.

stories.title: Florida has allocated $3 million to acquire a 642-acre property along the Suwannee River; officials say ending its current land use could save 159,000 gallons of water daily and reduce nutrient inputs
stories.summary: Florida has allocated $3 million for the acquisition of property along the Suwannee River to reduce water consumption. The Suwannee Sandhill Tract-Drew Property will help conserve approximately 158,800 gallons of water daily. This initiative is part of a larger $100 million investment aimed at various water conservation projects. The acquisition will facilitate the restoration of the land for wildlife habitats and public recreation.

Covering 4,368 square feet, the residence boasts four luxurious bedrooms and five opulent bathrooms. Dandridge's impactful legacy as a pioneering Black actress echoes through this property, complemented by breathtaking views of Los Angeles. The current owners have thoughtfully renovated it while respecting its historic charm.

Over the next three years, conservationists will introduce family groups of beavers to the area’s waterways, focusing on enhancing biodiversity and wildlife habitats, while also implementing strategies to resolve any conflicts with local farmers and landowners.

Chester Zoo's horticulturists are dedicated to preserving these rare species amidst growing environmental challenges. Currently, the orchids are not on public display but contribute to plant biodiversity conservation efforts.

The project has been under development since 2019 and will provide flood protection and recreational opportunities. A public meeting is scheduled for November 2026 to discuss construction details.

stories.title: A cupboard buried when Mount Vesuvius destroyed Pompeii in AD 79 has yielded 38 bronze coins and at least 24 tiny childhood charms; archaeologists say the objects reveal glimpses of a family's lost everyday life

It is speculated that the residents could not retrieve their belongings during the volcanic eruption.

stories.title: Veiled marble bust sells for record €1.925 million in Vienna

stories.title: US river straightened 110 years ago to drain land, now set for restoration to reduce floods
stories.summary: Authorities in Tennessee, US, have acquired 985 acres along the South Fork of the Forked Deer River to reduce flooding and restore natural habitats. The river was straightened in 1916 to drain surrounding land, but the changes contributed to flash floods and erosion. The restoration project aims to reconnect the river with its floodplain and eventually open the area to the public.

stories.title: A new fossil from China may reveal the first amphibian known to have lived entirely at sea; the armoured, 2.4-foot creature lived about 237 million years ago, challenging what scientists know about amphibian evolution
stories.summary: A recent discovery of the fossil Gerrothorax maritimus reveals that some ancient amphibians lived completely in marine environments. Dated to approximately 237 million years ago, this species had a flattened body covered in bony armour. The fossils were found in deep-sea sediments, indicating they lived far from landmasses. Geochemical tests confirmed the strontium isotopes matched those in seawater during the Late Triassic period.
